enGB: Gunslinger

For a renegade few, battle sounds different than it does for the typical fighter. The clash of steel and the sizzle of spell energy are drowned out by the thunderous rhythm of gunfire—the pounding beat of the gunslinger.

Gunslingers are a bold and mysterious lot. While many treat the secrets of black powder with the same care and reverence that a wizard typically reserves for his spellbook, most gunslingers know that firearms are a secret that cannot remain concealed forever. While current firearms are simple, often imprecise, and even dangerous devices, they are a technology on the move, and one that will become even more powerful when it is fully fused with magic.
Gunslinger Proficiencies
Gunslingers are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and with all firearms. They are proficient with all light armor.
Brave, clever, and frequently foolhardy gunslingers are thunderous artillery, often found where the fighting is fiercest.
Quick Clear

At 1st level, as a standard action, the gunslinger can remove the broken condition from a single firearm she is currently wielding, as long as that condition was gained by a firearm misfire. The gunslinger must have at least 1 grit point to perform this deed. Alternatively, if the gunslinger spends 1 grit point to perform this deed, she can perform quick clear as a move-equivalent action instead of a standard action.
Quick Clear (Standard)
As a standard action, the gunslinger can remove the broken condition from a single firearm she is currently wielding. The gunslinger must have at least 1 grit point to perform this deed.
Quick Clear (Move)
The gunslinger can remove the broken condition from a single firearm she is currently wielding as a move action if she spends 1 grit point.
Gunslinger Initiative
At 3rd level, as long as the gunslinger has at least 1 grit point, she gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks.
Targeting

At 7th level, as a full-round action, the gunslinger can make a single firearm attack and choose part of the body to target. She gains the following effects depending on the part of the body targeted. This deed costs 1 grit point to perform no matter which part of the creature she targets.

    Arms: On a hit, the target takes no damage from the hit but is disarmed.
    Head: On a hit, the target is damaged normally, and is also confused for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting effect.
    Legs: On a hit, the target is damaged normally and knocked prone.
Targeting (Headshot)
On a hit, the target is damaged normally, and is also confused for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting effect.
Targeting (Arms)
On a hit, the target takes no damage from the hit but is disarmed for 1 round plus 1 additional round for each 5 by which the hit roll exceeds their AC.
Targeting (Legs)
Legs: On a hit, the target is damaged normally and knocked prone.
Bleeding Shot

At 11th level, when the gunslinger hits a living creature with a firearm attack, she can spend 1 grit point as a free action to have that attack deal extra bleed damage. The amount of bleed damage is equal to the gunslinger's Dexterity modifier.
Bleeding Shot (Strength)
At 11th level, when the gunslinger hits a living creature with a firearm attack, she can spend 2 grit points as a free action to have that attack deal 1 point of Strength bleed damage.
Bleeding Shot (Constitution)
At 11th level, when the gunslinger hits a living creature with a firearm attack, she can spend 2 grit points as a free action to have that attack deal 1 point of Constitution bleed damage.
Bleeding Shot (Dexterity)
At 11th level, when the gunslinger hits a living creature with a firearm attack, she can spend 2 grit points as a free action to have that attack deal 1 point of Dexterity bleed damage.

At 11th level, when the gunslinger hits a living creature with a firearm attack, she can spend 1 grit point as a free action to have that attack deal extra bleed damage. The amount of bleed damage is equal to the gunslinger's Dexterity modifier. Alternatively, the gunslinger can spend 2 grit points to deal 1 point of Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution bleed damage (gunslinger's choice) instead.

Gunslinger's Evasion

At 15th level, when the gunslinger has at least 1 grit point, she gains the benefit of the evasion, uncanny dodge, and improved uncanny dodge rogue class features. She uses her gunslinger level as her rogue level for improved uncanny dodge.
Stunning Shot

At 19th level, when a gunslinger hits a creature, she can spend 2 grit points to stun the creature for 1 round. The creature must make a Fortitude saving throw (the DC = 10 + 1/2 the gunslinger's level + the gunslinger's Wisdom modifier). If the creature fails, it is stunned for 1 round.
Damaged Firearm

When a firearm misfires, it gains the broken condition. While it has the broken condition its misfire value increases by 2. If an early firearm with the broken condition misfires again, it explodes. Each firearm has a burst size noted in parentheses after its misfire value. Any creature within this burst (including the firearm's wielder) takes damage as if it had been hit by the weapon—a DC 12 Reflex save halves this damage.

If the natural result of your attack roll falls within a firearm's misfire value, that shot misses, even if you would have otherwise hit the target. Grit

A gunslinger makes her mark upon the world with daring deeds. Some gunslingers claim they belong to a mystical way of the gun, but it's more likely that the volatile nature of firearms simply prunes the unlucky and careless from their ranks. Whatever the reason, all gunslingers have grit. In game terms, grit is a fluctuating measure of a gunslinger's ability to perform amazing actions in combat. At the start of each day, a gunslinger gains a number of grit points equal to her Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Her grit goes up or down throughout the day, but usually cannot go higher than her Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), though some feats and magic items may affect this maximum. A gunslinger spends grit to accomplish deeds (see below), and regains grit in the following ways.

Critical Hit with a Firearm: Each time the gunslinger confirms a critical hit with a firearm attack while in the heat of combat, she regains 1 grit point.

Killing Blow with a Firearm: When the gunslinger reduces a creature to 0 or fewer hit points with a firearm attack while in the heat of combat, she regains 1 grit point.

At the start of each day, a gunslinger gains a number of grit points equal to her Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Her grit goes up or down throughout the day, but usually cannot go higher than her Wisdom modifier (minimum 1)
True Grit
At 20th level, a gunslinger recoveres 1 grit each time she spends it allowing her to perform deeds for 1 grit less so long as she has enough grit to perform them at their standard cost.
Gun Training
Starting at 5th level, a gunslinger gains a bonus equal to her Dexterity modifier on damage rolls with firearms.
Nimble

Starting at 2nd level, a gunslinger gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC while wearing light or no armor. Anything that causes the gunslinger to lose her Dexterity bonus to AC also causes the gunslinger to lose this dodge bonus. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd level (to a maximum of +5 at 20th level).
AC Bonus (Nimble)
Muzzle Loading

Early firearms are muzzle-loaded, requiring bullets or pellets and black powder to be rammed down the muzzle.. It is a standard action to load a one-handed early firearm and a full-round action to load a two-handed early firearm.
Chamber Loading

Advanced firearms are chamber-loaded. It is a move action to load a one-handed or two-handed advanced firearm to its full capacity. The Rapid Reload feat reduces this to a free action (allowing you to ignore the requirement to reload between shots).
Reload
Rapid Reload
Armor Penetrating
Firearms penetrate most forms of armor: bypassing shield, armor, and natural armor bonuses to AC
Musket

This long-barreled firearm has a much greater range than a pistol. A musket uses either a bullet and 1 dose of black powder or a single alchemical cartridge as its ammunition. This is an early firearm.
Pistol
The basic single-shot pistol is one of the most common firearms, although it is still rare enough to be an object of envy or curiosity to most. This is an early firearm.
Rifle

This improvement on the musket features a grooved barrel that imparts a twisting, spiral motion to the bullet as it exits, stabilizing it and preventing the end-over-end tumbling common to projectiles from simpler firearms. As a result, a rifle can fire significantly farther and with more accuracy than early long-bore firearms. A rifle uses metal cartridges as ammunition. This is an advanced firearm.
Revolver

A revolver is a pistol with a revolving cylinder containing six chambers. Each chamber can hold a metal cartridge, and when one cartridge is fired, the cylinder automatically rotates (no extra hand or action required), readying the next chamber for firing. A revolver uses metal cartridges as ammunition. This is an advanced firearm.
Weapon Proficiency (firearms)
The Weapon Proficiency (firearms) feat allows you to use all firearms without penalty.
Rapid Reload

The time required for you to reload a firearm is reduced to a move action (for a one-handed firearm), or a standard action (two-handed firearm). Reloading a firearm still provokes attacks of opportunity.

If you have this feat you may fire an advanced firearm as a full-attack action.

Finnean

Tough As Nails

At 20th level, if the Spellscar drifter confirms a critical hit on an attack made with a firearm, the target is stunned for 1d4 rounds. A successful Will saving throw (DC = 10 + the Spellscar drifter’s base attack bonus) reduces this effect to staggered instead of stunned
The Spellscar drifter can stun or stagger an enemy on a critical hit with a firearm.
Spell Severed
At 12th level, a Spellscar drifter becomes permanently marked by long exposure to the Spellscar Desert. The Spellscar drifter gains spell resistance equal to 10 + her character level.
The Spellscar drifter gains spell resistance equal to 10 + her character level.
Old Reliable

At 11th level, whenever a Spellscar drifter declares a challenge, the threat range of the Spellscar drifter’s firearm is doubled against the target of her challenge. This increase does not stack with other effects that double the threat range of the weapon.
The threat range of the Spellscar drifter’s firearms is doubled against the target of her challenge.
Spellscar Drifter

The Spellscar Desert is a dangerous wasteland into which few venture without a guide. Spellscar drifters have made themselves at home in these badlands. When not scouring the desert for forgotten treasures or magic hidden by the region’s shifting magic-dead zones, a Spellscar drifter might hire himself out as a guide, bodyguard, or assassin. There are even a few Spellscar drifters who are temporarily deputized by the Grand Duchy of Alkenstar to perform law enforcement tasks beyond the reach of the city’s normal constabulary. Spellscar drifters are self-reliant and always keep their firearms loaded—in the Spellscar Desert, a rider with a slow draw doesn’t live long.

There is something strange about this woman.
Order of the Eastern Star

This cavalier order exists to keep dangerous secrets hidden from the world and secretly protect the world against unimaginable threats from beyond the mortal realms. These cavaliers scout and observe, concerning themselves not with the trivial pursuit of morality, but rather with ensuring the survival of society itself. Edicts: The cavalier must preserve the secrets of his order while acting to protect civilization against occult threats. He must thwart the schemes of otherworldly horrors and must give his order a full accounting of any potential threats.
Challenge

Whenever a cavalier of the order of the eastern star issues a challenge, she receives a +1 dodge bonus to AC and a +1 insight bonus on saves against the attacks and abilities of the target of his challenge. She must be wearing light armor or no armor to receive these bonuses. These bonuses increase by 1 for every 4 class levels the cavalier possesses.
Skills
A cavalier belonging to the order of the eastern star adds Knowledge (arcana) to her class skills. She receives a bonus on Knowledge (arcana) checks equal to 1/2 his cavalier level (minimum +1).
Guarded

At 2nd level, the cavalier gains DR 1/— and a +2 morale bonus on saving throws when wearing light armor or no armor and fighting defensively or using Combat Expertise. At 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, this DR increases by 1.
Pierce the Guard

At 8th level, the cavalier's weapons are treated as having the cavalier's {g|Encyclopedia:Alignment}alignment{/g} for the purpose of overcoming the {g|Encyclopedia:Damage_Reduction}damage reduction{/g} of extraplaner creatures. Against an extraplaner target of her challenge, the cavalier automatically overcomes all damage reduction that creature possesses.
One Purpose

At 15th level, the cavalier’s mount shares the benefits of the cavalier’s guarded ability. The cavalier must fight defensively or use Combat Expertise to grant these benefits, but the mount need not. In addition, the mount gains all the benefits of the cavalier’s challenge.
Warp Space

Gateways between planes can warp the space around them interfering with normal teleportation yet to one with true understanding that distorted space can allow for a whole other kind of transport. This ability can be used at will and functions as dimension door however it can only be used while under the effects of Tear Proximity.

Bell
Lone Rider

One rarely enocunters a lone traveler in a place as harsh as the worldwound. Yet as the Commander crests a craggy hilltop that is exactly what {mf|he|she} finds. In the valley below a figure knees down in the dirt with an unnaturaly still horse by their side. Anywhere else such as sight would little more than an oddity yet here nothing is quite so simple. The sight of something so mundane sets the commander's company strangely on edge.
From the safety of the hilltop the Commander decides too...
... watch the stranger closely.
The Commander's keen eyes make out a body lying dead in the dirt. The stranger seems to be searching the body for something.
But the stranger is too far away to make out what their are doing.
...try and identify the stranger.

The unusual clothes and weapons worn by the stranger marks her out as a native of Alkenstar a nation in Garund famous for it's advanced technology. Most notably it is one of the few places which holds the secrets of gunsmithing. Allowing them to create powerful firearms such she bears.
The unusual clothes and weaponry worn by the stranger suggests they're not from around here but the Commander has never seen the like of them before.
...sense the air for any sign of illusions.
It's hard to tell amidst the raw chaos of the Worldwound but there is a trace of something in the air. There was magic here but whatever it was it's gone now.
Any signs of magic are lost amidst the raw chaos of the Wound.
...move in closer.

It would seem the Commander is not the only one interested in this strange precence within the Wound. From the scant cover of withering vegetation the Commander spots a motly gang of demons and cultists creeping through the valley towards the stranger.
Still possessing the element of surprise the Commander...
...charges into the fray.

The Commander bursts into the fray meeting the demons head on. The sudden onslaught catches the demons off guard inflicting serious damage and forcing them back into the valley wall. Even so the Commander is greatly outnumbered and slowly the battle begins to turn against {mf|him|her}

The slope proves rougher than expected and the Commander is exhuasted before {mf|he|she} even reaches the bottom. When the two forces meet the demons hold their ground and begin to push the Commander back uphill.
...clambers down the rockface to outflank the enemy.

The Commander slips around and strikes the enemy from the rear inflicting serious damage and forcing them back into the valley wall. Even so the Commander is greatly outnumbered and slowly the battle begins to turn against {mf|him|her}

The slope proves rougher than expected and the Commander is exhuasted before {mf|he|she} even reaches the bottom. When the two forces meet the demons hold their ground and begin to push the Commander back uphill.

A sudden bang as loud as thunder echoes through the valley. Metal pellets rend through demon hide as the stranger joins the battle. For a moment everything seems to slow as all eyes turn to the newcomer and the smoking metal rod in her hands.
"So these are demons then ey? Seem they'll bleed just like the rest of us." she mutters before firing again.
With the strangers help the tide turns in the Commander's favour and the demons soon lie dead and {mf|his|her} feet.
As the smoke clears the stranger steps forward "Thanks for the help there. Bell Tarvil, Shieldmarshal of Alkenstar at your service" she tips her hat the commanders way.
Offer a hand: "I'm {name} pleasure to make your acquaintance"
"You fought well yourself. I'm {name} Commander of the Fifth Crusade"

"Ah so you're the one I heard about back in Kenebres. Things are rough back there but I reckon they'd've been worse without your help. Anyway you're probably wondering what brings a gal like me all the way out here all by my lonesome. I'm on the trail of a villain. He's a real monster who loves to delve into all the worst kinds of magic, alchemy and any other kind of dark knowledge he can get his hands on."
"Who is he?"
"Is he working with the demons?"
"What makes him so important to travel halfway around the world for?"
"Is there anything I can do to help?"
"Would you consider joining the crusade?"
"He's taken to calling himself the Brainweaver. He's a master of the twisted art of fleshwarping and head of a cult of crazies who think he understands the mysteries of reality or some such rot."
